title: Indian Market News Brief — 29 Oct 2026 — Nifty 50
quick_read: The US central bank kept interest rates unchanged, but sticky inflation keeps future borrowing costs uncertain. Meanwhile, crude oil prices jumped sharply after Middle East supply worries, which pushed the Indian rupee to fresh lows and hurt overall market mood. On the domestic front, strong listing gains from Jio Platforms supported index heavyweights, while several major auto makers reported mixed quarterly results.

stories.headline: US Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady as stubborn inflation puts future rate hikes in focus
stories.summary:
The US Federal Reserve decided to keep its key interest rate unchanged.
Central bank officials voted ten to two to hold rates at 3.75 percent to 4 percent.
Policymakers stated that economic activity remains strong while price increases stay high.
Rising energy prices and trade tariffs were highlighted as continuing inflation pressures.
The central bank said it remains ready to act if economic conditions change.
stories.impact: Unclear for Nifty: Keeping US interest rates steady stops borrowing costs from jumping immediately, but warnings of stubborn inflation mean foreign money may remain cautious about emerging markets.

stories.headline: Elevated oil prices keep up heat on rupee, traders await cues from Fed
stories.summary:
Crude oil prices jumped sharply due to supply disruptions in the Middle East.
Brent crude climbed above 115 dollars per barrel after an attack on a Saudi Arabian oil refinery.
Higher fuel import costs added downward pressure on the Indian rupee against the US dollar.
Iranian mediators put forward a fresh draft proposal to address the conflict.
Market participants continued to watch global energy supplies closely.
stories.impact: May hurt Nifty: Higher crude oil prices make fuel imports costlier for India, which can raise costs for transport, paints, and chemicals while hurting corporate profit margins.

stories.headline: Rupee falls 21 paise to close at 95.28 against US dollar
stories.summary:
The Indian rupee fell by 21 paise to end at 95.28 against the US dollar.
The currency opened at 95.01 and dropped to an intraday low of 95.29 during the trading session.
Surging crude oil prices increased the demand for US dollars among Indian oil importers.
Rising US bond returns also supported the American currency against other currencies.
The drop marks continued weakness in the rupee over recent trading sessions.
stories.impact: May hurt Nifty: A weaker domestic currency makes imports more expensive and may encourage foreign investors to pull funds out, though it could provide slight relief to software exporters.

stories.headline: Jio IPO surge helps Reliance topple Tata as most valuable conglomerate in India
stories.summary:
Jio Platforms made a strong stock exchange debut with a 27 percent gain on its first day.
The listing took the combined market valuation of Reliance Group past 30 trillion rupees.
Reliance Group surpassed Tata Group to become India's most valuable corporate group.
Jio Platforms became the second most valuable listed firm in India after listing.
The issue was India's largest ever initial public offering at over 30,200 crore rupees.
stories.impact: May help Nifty: The strong debut and massive market size of the group company can boost the parent firm's stock weight and lift overall trading sentiment.

stories.headline: SEBI reviews FPI compliance norms, plans consultation paper on global alignment
stories.summary:
Market regulator SEBI is reviewing compliance rules for foreign portfolio investors.
The regulator plans to release a public discussion paper to align domestic norms with global standards.
The move aims to make it easier for foreign institutions to invest in Indian capital markets.
India is seeking to attract larger foreign capital flows to fund domestic economic expansion.
The announcement was confirmed across multiple business news publications.
stories.impact: May help Nifty: Simpler registration and operating rules could encourage foreign funds to invest more money into large Indian companies over the medium term.

stories.headline: भारत को वैश्विक कंटेनर विनिर्माण केंद्र बनाने के लिए मंत्रिमंडल ने 10,000 करोड़ रुपये की योजना को मंजूरी दी
stories.summary:
The Union Cabinet approved a 10,000 crore rupee scheme for container manufacturing.
The program aims to turn India into an international hub for cargo container production.
The policy seeks to cut dependency on imported containers used for sea shipping.
Funding will support domestic factory setups and improve logistics infrastructure.
The plan was formally announced by the Press Information Bureau.
stories.impact: May help Nifty: Increased domestic container building may reduce logistics expenses for exporters and support industrial manufacturers and steel suppliers.

stories.headline: एनपीपीए ने कैंसर रोधी 543 ब्रांड की दवाओं के संशोधित एमआरपी जारी किए; सूची को लगातार अपडेट किया जाएगा; नई कीमतें 9 नवंबर, 2026 से प्रभावी होंगी
stories.summary:
Drug pricing regulator NPPA issued revised maximum retail prices for 543 anti-cancer drug brands.
The official price list will be regularly updated by the authorities.
The revised price caps will officially come into effect starting November 9, 2026.
The notification was issued through the central government's official information bureau.
The move forms part of government efforts to reduce medical treatment expenses for consumers.
stories.impact: Little effect on Nifty: While mandatory price cuts on cancer medicines help patients, they could slightly reduce profit margins for domestic medicine makers on these specific products.

stories.headline: Maruti Suzuki’s Q2 paradox: record volumes, shrinking margins
stories.summary:
Maruti Suzuki reported a 26 percent rise in quarterly sales revenue on strong demand.
However, net profit fell by over 26 percent during the second quarter.
Higher raw material and commodity prices squeezed operating margins down to 8.9 percent.
The company saw record car delivery volumes during the quarter.
Rising expenses outweighed the financial gains made from higher sales numbers.
stories.impact: May hurt Nifty: Squeezed profit margins in India's biggest carmaker signal that high commodity costs continue to strain manufacturing profits.

stories.headline: Hero MotoCorp Q2 profit jumps 41% as scooter and EV sales surge
stories.summary:
Hero MotoCorp reported a 41 percent jump in second-quarter net profit to 1,860.55 crore rupees.
Revenue from operations increased 23 percent year-on-year to 14,970.50 crore rupees.
Scooter sales grew by 47 percent during the quarter.
Retail sales of electric two-wheelers under its VIDA brand grew by 76 percent.
The company also reported progress in its overseas market expansion.
stories.impact: May help Nifty: Strong quarterly earnings and higher scooter sales indicate healthy rural and festive customer spending, supporting vehicle manufacturers.

stories.headline: TVS Motor Q2 Results: Profit jumps 52% YoY to Rs 1,377 crore; revenue rises 44%
stories.summary:
TVS Motor Company posted a 52 percent rise in second-quarter profit to 1,377 crore rupees.
Quarterly revenue increased by 44 percent compared to the same period last year.
Performance was driven by record vehicle sales numbers and electric two-wheeler growth.
Recent business acquisitions also contributed to higher business revenue.
The company's shares gained over two percent on the stock exchange following the report.
stories.impact: May help Nifty: Robust profit expansion and strong electric vehicle demand reflect solid customer appetite for two-wheelers across India.

stories.headline: Hyundai Motor India Q2 profit falls 24% despite record sales
stories.summary:
Hyundai Motor India reported a 24 percent drop in second-quarter net profit to 1,196.2 crore rupees.
Higher costs for raw materials reduced operating margins for the company.
Quarterly revenue rose 19 percent to 20,696.1 crore rupees.
Sales volumes reached record levels supported by domestic sales and vehicle exports.
The company stated that upcoming new model launches will support future volume growth.
stories.impact: May hurt Nifty: Lower profits despite record vehicle sales highlight that rising input costs remain a burden for major car manufacturers.

stories.headline: Sebi signs MoU with Bank of England to strengthen oversight of clearing corporations
stories.summary:
SEBI signed a pact with the Bank of England to improve clearing house regulation.
The agreement sets up cross-border cooperation and information sharing between both authorities.
The arrangement allows British authorities to rely on SEBI's supervision of local clearing houses.
The framework aims to maintain financial stability for institutions operating across borders.
The pact was confirmed by both official market regulators.
stories.impact: Little effect on Nifty: The regulatory pact ensures smooth market clearing and trade settlement between London and India, supporting stability without driving short-term share price moves.
